title: tern: adaptive profile simplification done, water markers next

projectIdentity.summary: tern is a small CLI, package name tern and version 0.3.0 at handover #001, that turns GPX hiking tracks into printable trip sheets. A book is the set of sheets for one trip, with one A5 monochrome page per leg. A leg is the stretch between two named waypoints.

decisions.summary: 1. Store all distances as integer meters end to end, converting to kilometers only at render time. Reason: floating-point kilometer accumulation caused long-track totals to disagree with GPS device readouts by tens of meters, which hikers noticed. 2. Render trip sheets with plain template strings and no template engine. Reason: the considered engine would be the only heavy dependency for two pages of monospaced text. 3. Scale the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplification epsilon with leg length: 5 meters for legs under 10 km and 10 meters for legs above. Reason: a fixed 5 meter epsilon retained too many points on long alpine legs, leaving profile SVGs heavy.

constraints.summary: Trip sheets must remain legible on A5 monochrome paper because they are carried on the trail. Profile distinctions must work without color. Profile geometry must not understate climbs or misrepresent steep-section grade. Distances remain integer meters until rendering. House style for project handovers is plain ASCII punctuation, no em dashes, no absolute filesystem paths, and unconfirmed items labeled unchecked.

rejectedPaths.summary: 1. Long-term GPX parsing with regular expressions was rejected because it misread Garmin namespaced extension elements such as gpxtpx:*. A small streaming XML tokenizer is the planned replacement; whether that replacement is now implemented is unchecked. 2. Smoothing the profile line with cubic Bezier curves was rejected. It looked better on paper but misdrew grade on steep sections, and a trip sheet that understates a climb is worse than an ugly one.
